mainTopic: Which ages of birds are fit for a קרבן: grown תורים, young בני יונה, and the unfit yellowing stage in between
overview: This amud deals with which ages of birds may be brought as a קרבן. A ברייתא teaches that תורים (turtledoves) are fit only when grown and בני יונה (young pigeons) only when young. For each rule it first suggests a קל וחומר that would allow the other age, then says the פסוק blocks it. רבא shows the source: the Torah always writes plain 'תורים' and 'בני יונה' and never switches the wording. The גמרא challenges that this only limits the pigeons, and answers that the two birds are compared, so each has one fixed age. Another ברייתא learns from the word 'מן' that the in-between stage, the start of the yellowing, is unfit for both birds. It gives color signs, and יעקב קרחה and אביי add when young pigeons first become fit: when a plucked feather draws blood. Finally רבי זירא asks whether the yellowing stage is a ספק or a separate בריה, and רבא tries to prove from the פסוק's exclusion that it is a בריה.

steps.title: Turtledoves must be grown, not young
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא suggests a קל וחומר that young תורים should be valid, then rejects it: the פסוק says 'תורים', meaning grown birds only.
steps.simpleTranslation: If young pigeons, which are not fit when grown, are fit when young, then turtledoves, which are fit when grown, should surely be fit when young too! That is why the verse says 'turtledoves': grown ones, not young ones.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא is finishing its first rule: תורים are only valid as a קרבן when they are grown. It shows a logical argument someone might make, and then says the פסוק blocks it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The argument is a קל וחומר: בני יונה are the 'weaker' bird (not valid when grown), yet they are valid when young. So תורים, the 'stronger' bird (valid when grown), should be valid when young as well. The ברייתא says no, because the פסוק limits תורים to grown birds.

keyTerms.meaning: Turtledoves; valid for a קרבן only when grown
Young pigeons; valid for a קרבן only when young
Were made fit (valid) for a קרבן
Isn't it logical? Opens the ending of a קל וחומר
The verse says: the פסוק teaches otherwise

steps.confusionAlert: Don't mix up the two birds: תורים are valid only when GROWN, בני יונה are valid only when YOUNG. They are opposites.

phrases.aramaic: וּמָה בְּנֵי יוֹנָה שֶׁלֹּא הוּכְשְׁרוּ בִּגְדוֹלִים
phrases.english: Now if young pigeons, which were not made fit when grown,
phrases.notes: 'Made fit' means valid to bring as a קרבן.

phrases.english: were made fit when young,
then turtledoves, which were made fit when grown,
isn't it logical that they should be made fit when young?
Therefore the verse says: 'Turtledoves',
grown ones and not young ones.

steps.triggerLanguage: וּמָה בְּנֵי יוֹנָה שֶׁלֹּא הוּכְשְׁרוּ בִּגְדוֹלִים הוּכְשְׁרוּ בִּקְטַנִּים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes the first half of the ברייתא that began just before this section.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: תורים are valid only when grown; the פסוק blocks a קל וחומר that would allow young ones.

steps.title: Young pigeons must be young, not grown
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא gives the mirror rule: בני יונה only when young. It suggests a קל וחומר allowing grown ones, then rejects it from the פסוק.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'Young pigeons': young ones and not grown ones. Because one might think: isn't it logical? If turtledoves, which are not fit when young, are fit when grown, then young pigeons, which are fit when young, should surely be fit when grown! That is why the verse says 'young pigeons': young ones, not grown ones.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא now gives the second rule, the exact mirror of the first: בני יונה are valid only when young.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This time the קל וחומר goes the other way. תורים are not valid when young but are valid when grown, so בני יונה, which are valid when young, should also be valid when grown. The word 'בני' ('young ones of') in the פסוק blocks this.

keyTerms.meaning: Isn't it logical? Opens a קל וחומר

steps.whatToRemember: The ברייתא's two rules: תורים only when grown, בני יונה only when young. Logic alone would have allowed both ages, but the פסוק limits each bird.

phrases.english: 'Young pigeons': young ones and not grown ones,
for one might have thought: isn't it logical?
If turtledoves, which were not made fit when young,
were made fit when grown,
then young pigeons, which were made fit when young,
isn't it logical that they should be made fit when grown?
Therefore the verse says: 'Young pigeons',
young ones and not grown ones.

steps.triggerLanguage: בְּנֵי יוֹנָה קְטַנִּים וְלֹא גְּדוֹלִים שֶׁיָּכוֹל וַהֲלֹא דִּין הוּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the mirror-image rule for the second bird.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: בני יונה are valid only when young; the פסוק blocks a קל וחומר that would allow grown ones.

steps.title: Where exactly does the verse teach this?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks how the פסוק actually shows these age limits.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks where the פסוק really teaches these rules. This question sets up רבא's answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For בני יונה, the word 'בני' hints at young birds. But the word 'תורים' alone doesn't obviously say 'grown only'. So the גמרא wants to know how the ברייתא reads this from the verse.

keyTerms.meaning: The learning or source: how the rule is drawn from the verse

phrases.english: What is the derivation?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the textual source behind both rules of the ברייתא.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: How the פסוק teaches that תורים must be grown and בני יונה must be young.

steps.title: רבא: the Torah never switches the wording
steps.stepSummary: רבא answers that the Torah always says 'תורים' and 'בני יונה' and never 'young turtledoves' or plain 'pigeon', which shows each bird has a set age.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: The verse never strays and writes 'of young turtledoves or of pigeons'.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא answers the question. The proof is a steady pattern in how the Torah words these birds.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Everywhere, the Torah adds 'בני' (young) only to the pigeons, and never to the turtledoves. If both ages were fine for both birds, we would expect the wording to switch sometimes. Since it never does, תורים must be grown and בני יונה must be young.

keyTerms.meaning: To slip away or stray: to break from the usual wording

phrases.english: Rava said:
The verse never strays
phrases.notes: He means the Torah always uses the same pattern: plain 'turtledoves' and 'YOUNG pigeons'.

phrases.aramaic: וְלִכְתּוֹב ״מִן בְּנֵי הַתּוֹרִים אוֹ מִן הַיּוֹנָה״.
phrases.english: and writes 'of young turtledoves, or of pigeons'.

steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The Torah's constant wording ('תורים' never with 'בני', 'יונה' always with 'בני') shows each bird has a fixed age.

steps.title: Maybe turtledoves can be any age
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges: the word 'בני' only limits pigeons to young ones; maybe turtledoves are fine at any age.
steps.simpleTranslation: Say instead: young pigeons, about which the Merciful One wrote 'young', yes when young, no when grown. But turtledoves: if he wants, let him bring grown ones, and if he wants, let him bring young ones!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back on רבא's proof. It agrees the word 'בני' limits pigeons, but says nothing in the wording limits turtledoves.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word 'בני' is written only next to the pigeons. So it makes sense that pigeons must be young. But the plain word 'תורים' has no limit at all, so maybe a person can bring turtledoves at any age.

keyTerms.meaning: Say instead: offers another way to read things
The Merciful One: a name for ה׳ as the Giver of the Torah

phrases.english: Say instead: young pigeons,
about which the Merciful One wrote 'young',
young ones yes, grown ones no;
but turtledoves: if he wants, let him bring grown ones,
and if he wants, let him bring young ones!

steps.triggerLanguage: אֵימָא בְּנֵי יוֹנָה דִּכְתַב בְּהוּ רַחֲמָנָא בְּנֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רבא's reading as only proving half the rule.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבא's proof that תורים must be grown.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The word 'בני' limits only pigeons; nothing in the wording limits turtledoves, so they could be any age.

steps.title: The two birds are compared to each other
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers: turtledoves are compared to pigeons. Just as pigeons have a fixed age (young only), turtledoves also have a fixed age (grown only).
steps.simpleTranslation: It is like young pigeons: just as young pigeons are fit when young but not when grown, so too turtledoves are fit when grown but not when young.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא defends רבא by comparing the two birds. Each one has only one age that works.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Since the birds are compared, whatever kind of rule pigeons have, turtledoves have too. Pigeons have a strict, one-age-only rule, so turtledoves must also have a one-age-only rule. Since the Torah never calls them 'young', their one age must be grown.

keyTerms.meaning: Similar to, like: the two are compared
Just as ... so too: the form of a comparison

steps.whatToRemember: Final rule: תורים only grown, בני יונה only young. The Torah's steady wording, plus comparing the two birds, teaches that each bird has one fixed age.

phrases.english: It is similar to young pigeons:
just as young pigeons:
young ones yes, grown ones no,
so too turtledoves:
grown ones yes, young ones no.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 5 and keeps רבא's proof standing.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Comparison (היקש-style): the birds share the same kind of rule.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Turtledoves have no age limit, since only pigeons are called 'בני'.
steps.terutzMaskana: Just as pigeons have one fixed age, turtledoves do too: grown only.

steps.title: Not every turtledove or pigeon is fit: the yellowing stage is excluded
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא learns from the word 'מן' that birds at the start of the yellowing stage are unfit both as תורים and as בני יונה.
steps.simpleTranslation: The Sages taught: You might think every turtledove and every young pigeon is fit. So the פסוק says 'from the turtledoves', meaning not all of them, and 'from the young pigeons', meaning not all of them. This leaves out a bird at the start of the yellowing stage, which is unfit as either type.
steps.whatsHappening: A new ברייתא teaches that there is an in-between age when a bird is unfit as either a turtledove or a young pigeon.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word 'מן' ('from') means only part of the group, not all of it. The part left out is the stage when the neck feathers start to turn yellow. At that point the bird is too old to count as a young pigeon and too young to count as a grown turtledove.

keyTerms.meaning: 'From'. It means 'some of', not all, so it signals that part of the group is left out.
The beginning of the yellowing: the stage when the neck feathers start turning yellow

steps.confusionAlert: The same yellowing stage is unfit for both birds, for opposite reasons. For a pigeon it is too late, and for a turtledove it is too early.

phrases.english: The Sages taught:
One might think that all turtledoves would be
and all young pigeons would be fit?
Therefore the verse says: 'from the turtledoves'
and not all turtledoves,

phrases.aramaic: ״מִן בְּנֵי הַיּוֹנָה״ – וְלֹא כׇּל בְּנֵי יוֹנָה,
phrases.english: 'from the young pigeons', and not all young pigeons,
leaving out the beginning of the yellowing
phrases.notes: This is the stage when the bird's neck feathers first start to turn yellow.

phrases.english: of this one and of that one, which is unfit.

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּנוּ רַבָּנַן: יָכוֹל יְהוּ כׇּל הַתּוֹרִים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After setting that each bird has a fixed age, a new ברייתא marks the in-between stage that is unfit for both.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A bird at the beginning of the yellowing stage is unfit both as a turtledove and as a young pigeon, learned from the word 'מן'.

steps.title: The color signs: gold for turtledoves, yellow for pigeons
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא gives the signs: turtledoves become fit once they turn gold, and young pigeons become unfit once they turn yellow.
steps.simpleTranslation: From when are turtledoves fit? From when they turn gold. From when are young pigeons unfit? From when they turn yellow.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא continues and gives clear color signs for the start and end of each bird's fit age.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Yellowing is the end point for בני יונה. Turning a shining gold, which comes later, is the start point for תורים. The gap between these two colors is the excluded in-between stage from the last step.

keyTerms.meaning: 'From when?' It asks at what point something begins.

phrases.english: From when are turtledoves fit?
From when they turn gold.
From when are young pigeons unfit?
From when they turn yellow.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: It defines in practical signs the age limits behind the excluded stage of step 7.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Turtledoves are fit from when they turn gold. Young pigeons are unfit from when they turn yellow.

steps.title: יעקב קרחה: pigeons become fit once they reach the stage of 'יעלעו'
steps.stepSummary: יעקב קרחה teaches the lower age limit for young pigeons, using an unusual word that he explains from a פסוק in איוב.
steps.simpleTranslation: יעקב קרחה taught: From when are young pigeons fit? From when they 'יעלעו'. He taught it and he also explained it, from the verse 'Its chicks suck up (יעלעו) blood.'
steps.whatsHappening: A new source gives the starting point for young pigeons: before this stage they are too young to be brought at all.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The earlier ברייתא gave only the end point for pigeons (yellowing). יעקב קרחה adds the start point. He uses the rare word 'יעלעו', and he himself shows its meaning from a פסוק that ties it to blood.

keyTerms.meaning: A rare word connected to sucking up blood. It marks a stage of the young bird's growth.

keyTerms.term: הוּא תָנֵי לַהּ וְהוּא אָמַר לַהּ
keyTerms.meaning: He taught the rule and he himself explained it

phrases.english: Yaakov Korcha taught:
From when are young pigeons fit?
From when they 'ye'alu'.

phrases.aramaic: הוּא תָנֵי לַהּ וְהוּא אָמַר לַהּ,
phrases.english: He taught it and he explained it:
'Its chicks suck up blood.'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: It adds the lower age limit for young pigeons, which step 8 did not give.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Young pigeons are fit from the stage called 'יעלעו'.

steps.title: When exactly is that stage?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what point in practice matches the 'יעלעו' stage.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks for a practical way to tell when the 'יעלעו' stage arrives. This sets up אביי's answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A פסוק about chicks and blood does not tell us how to check a real bird. The גמרא wants a test someone can actually use.

phrases.english: When is that?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: It asks for a practical definition of יעקב קרחה's term.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: A practical sign that shows when a young pigeon has reached the 'יעלעו' stage.

steps.title: אביי: when a plucked feather brings out blood
steps.stepSummary: אביי explains that the stage arrives when plucking a feather from the bird makes blood come out.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said: From when a person plucks a feather from it and blood comes out.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי gives a simple test: pull a feather, and if blood comes out, the pigeon is old enough.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This connects the פסוק's 'blood' to something you can see. Once the feathers have blood in them, the bird has grown enough to be a fit young pigeon.
steps.whatToRemember: Young pigeons are fit from when a plucked feather draws blood, until they start to yellow. Turtledoves are fit only from when they turn gold. The yellowing stage in between is unfit for both.

phrases.english: Abaye said:
From when one plucks a feather from it
and blood comes out.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר אַבָּיֵי: מִכִּי שָׁמֵיט גַּדְפָּא מִינֵיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: It answers the question of step 10.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The stage begins when plucking a feather causes blood to come out.

steps.title: רבי זירא asks: is the yellowing stage a doubt or a separate creature?
steps.stepSummary: רבי זירא asks about someone who vowed an עולה of birds and brought one of each type at the yellowing stage. Is that stage a ספק (so bringing both works), or a separate בריה (so neither works)?
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי זירא asked: Someone says, 'I take upon myself an עולה of turtledoves or of young pigeons,' and he brought birds at the start of the yellowing, one of each kind. What is the law? Is this stage a doubt, so he has fulfilled his vow? Or is it a creature of its own, so he has not?
steps.whatsHappening: A new question opens about what the yellowing stage really is, using a case where the answer makes a practical difference.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the stage is a ספק, each bird is really either 'old' or 'young'. Then one of the two birds he brought must be fit, so he is covered. If it is a בריה, a category of its own, then neither bird counts and he has not fulfilled his vow.

keyTerms.meaning: 'I take upon myself an עולה'. This is the wording of a vow (נדר) to bring a burnt offering.
A doubt. Here it means the bird really belongs to one group, but we don't know which.
A creature of its own: a separate category, neither old nor young

steps.confusionAlert: He brought two birds, a turtledove and a pigeon, both at the yellowing stage. That is why a ספק would help him: whichever way the doubt goes, one of the two birds is fit.

phrases.english: Rabbi Zeira asked:
One who says: 'I take upon myself a burnt offering

phrases.aramaic: מִן הַתּוֹרִים אוֹ מִן בְּנֵי הַיּוֹנָה״,
phrases.english: of turtledoves or of young pigeons,'
and he brought birds at the beginning of the yellowing
of this kind and of that kind. What is the law?
phrases.notes: He brought one turtledove and one pigeon, both at the yellowing stage.

phrases.english: Is it a doubt, so he fulfills his vow,
or perhaps it is a creature of its own,
so he does not fulfill his vow?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: It builds on the excluded yellowing stage of step 7 and asks what its true nature is.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Is the yellowing stage a doubt between the two ages, or a separate category of its own?

steps.title: רבא: the פסוק's exclusion shows it is a separate creature
steps.stepSummary: רבא argues from the ברייתא: if the stage were only a ספק, the Torah would not need a פסוק to exclude it. So it must be a בריה.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: Come and hear. The ברייתא says the פסוק excludes the start of the yellowing of both kinds as unfit. If you say it is a creature of its own, that works well. But if you say it is a doubt, would a פסוק be needed to exclude a doubt?
steps.whatsHappening: רבא brings a proof from the ברייתא in step 7 to answer רבי זירא's question.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A doubtful bird could not be brought anyway, simply because of the doubt, so a פסוק would add nothing. Since the Torah did go out of its way to exclude this stage, רבא concludes that it is a separate בריה. If so, bringing one of each kind would not work.

keyTerms.meaning: 'Granted', 'it makes sense'. It introduces the option that fits well.

steps.whyThisMatters: The proof depends on a basic rule of learning: the Torah does not write a פסוק to teach something we would know anyway. So an exclusion must be teaching something new.

phrases.english: Rava said: Come and hear:
'leaving out the beginning of the yellowing'
phrases.notes: He is quoting the ברייתא from step 7.

phrases.english: 'of this one and of that one, which is unfit.'
Granted, if you say
it is a creature of its own, that works well.
But if you say it is a doubt,
would a verse be needed to exclude a doubt?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: It tries to settle רבי זירא's question in step 12 using the ברייתא of step 7.
steps.raayaObject: That the yellowing stage is a separate בריה, so one who brought one of each kind has not fulfilled his vow.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The ברייתא's teaching that a פסוק excludes the yellowing stage. A פסוק would not be needed to exclude a mere doubt.
